question: Find the value of: 66−⁵ ÷ 66¹¹ × 66−¹²
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For operations on terms with the same base, exponents are combined directly according to BODMAS.

Power for division is subtracted and for multiplication is added: am ÷ aⁿ × ap = am − ⁿ ⁺ p.

Given base is 66, combining the exponents directly:

Resulting power = −5 − 11 + (−12) = −28.

**∴ The correct answer is 66−²⁸.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

66−⁵ ÷ 66¹¹ × 66−¹²

**Formula Used:**

Quotient rule: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ

Product rule: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ

**Calculation:**

⇒ According to the order of operations (BODMAS), division and multiplication are evaluated from left to right.

⇒ First, evaluate the division part: (66−⁵ ÷ 66¹¹)

⇒ 66−⁵ − ¹¹ × 66−¹²

⇒ 66−¹⁶ × 66−¹²

⇒ Now, apply the product rule for multiplication:

⇒ 66−¹⁶ ⁺ ⁽−¹²⁾

⇒ 66−²⁸

**∴ The correct answer is 66−²⁸.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of Exponents

When multiplying expressions with the same base, add their exponents together: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ.

Quotient Rule of Exponents

When dividing expressions with the same base, subtract the exponent of the divisor from the exponent of the dividend: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ.

Negative Exponent Rule

A negative exponent indicates the reciprocal of the base raised to the positive opposite of the power: a−ⁿ = 1 ÷ aⁿ.

Power of a Power Rule

When an exponential expression is raised to another power, multiply the two exponents together: (am)ⁿ = am×ⁿ.
